record.paper_title: Cooperative Games with Incomplete Information: Some Open Problems
record.context_brief: Second-best coco without ex post observability
record.original_question: In environments where types or payoffs do not satisfy the ex post observability assumptions used to obtain first-best implementation results, can one construct a second-best analog of the coco solution that remains appropriate under incomplete information?

evidence.quote: A. Kalai and E. Kalai (2011) point out the following open problems: extension of the coco value in the TU case for more than two players and in the NTU case for two players or more, and construction of a second best analog of the coco value for environments that do not satisfy ex post observability conditions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider two-player Bayesian games with transferable utility in which each player privately observes a type drawn from a commonly known joint distribution and chooses an action; payoffs depend on the action profile and the type profile. In the special setting where realized types or payoffs are eventually observable ex post (so that contracts can be made contingent on this realization), the cooperative-competitive (coco) value provides a canonical, axiomatically justified first-best solution that combines an efficient cooperative component with a minmax-based competitive component.

Drop the ex post observability assumption: assume that after play one cannot verify the realized types or payoffs, so any agreement among the players must be incentive compatible with respect to their private information.

Problem. Construct a "second-best" analog of the coco value for two-player (and more generally n-player) Bayesian games with transferable utility that do not satisfy ex post observability, in the following sense:

(i) Specify a domain of Bayesian games and a class of mechanisms (interim individually rational, Bayesian incentive compatible, budget-balanced transfer schemes) on which the solution is defined.

(ii) Define a single-valued solution concept that assigns to each such game an interim expected payoff vector, reducing to the coco value when ex post observability holds and first-best implementation is feasible.

(iii) Provide an axiomatic characterization (analogues of Pareto efficiency on the second-best frontier, symmetry, covariance under affine utility transformations, monotonicity in information, and a competitive/threat component) that uniquely determines the solution.

Either exhibit such a solution and prove its characterization, or prove that no solution satisfying a stated list of natural axioms exists.
artifact.status_search_result: Web search did not turn up a published construction of a second-best coco value for environments without ex post observability. Subsequent work on cooperative analysis of incomplete information (e.g., Qingmin Liu's notes, 2023) and on the coco value continues to treat this as an outstanding direction, and no axiomatic second-best analog of the coco value appears to have been established.

status_evidence.title: The Cooperative-Competitive Value (Kalai & Kalai)
status_evidence.snippet: The coco value is defined under ex post observability of payoffs/types; first-best implementation is obtained via state-contingent transfers.
status_evidence.claim: The coco value framework relies on ex post observability, leaving the no-observability case unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Cooperative Analysis of Incomplete Information (Q. Liu, 2023)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey notes discussing cooperative solutions under incomplete information; a second-best coco analog without ex post observability is not presented as resolved.
status_evidence.claim: No established second-best coco analog is reported in recent surveys.
